decisions.reason: A catalog variant close to the core offer costs little to keep listed, and one year of results has not yet resolved how much demand there is for an adjustable quarter-pallet display, so the option stays open.
The pegboard-back shelf display uses existing cardboard capabilities and costs little to keep on the website, and its value is still uncertain after only one year.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format with likely steady demand and negligible holding cost, so there is no evidence that would justify abandoning it.
The eighth-pallet display completes the firm's format range at minimal marginal cost, and its prospects are not yet clear enough to drop it.
The wooden pallet moves beyond the core paper business and may cost more to sustain, but its uncertain value as a diversification option justifies keeping it open for now.
The media-specific display serves a niche that may be shrinking, but keeping it costs little and its results are not yet conclusive.
